From ec3937107ab43f3e8b2bc9dad95710043c462ff7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Baoquan He <bhe@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2019 10:03:13 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] x86/mm/KASLR: Fix the size of the direct mapping section

kernel_randomize_memory() uses __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT to calculate
the maximum amount of system RAM supported. The size of the direct
mapping section is obtained from the smaller one of the below two
values:

  (actual system RAM size + padding size) vs (max system RAM size supported)

This calculation is wrong since commit

  b83ce5ee9147 ("x86/mm/64: Make __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT always 52").

In it, __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT was changed to be 52, regardless of whether
the kernel is using 4-level or 5-level page tables. Thus, it will always
use 4 PB as the maximum amount of system RAM, even in 4-level paging
mode where it should actually be 64 TB.

Thus, the size of the direct mapping section will always
be the sum of the actual system RAM size plus the padding size.

Even when the amount of system RAM is 64 TB, the following layout will
still be used. Obviously KALSR will be weakened significantly.

   |____|_______actual RAM_______|_padding_|______the rest_______|
   0            64TB                                            ~120TB

Instead, it should be like this:

   |____|_______actual RAM_______|_________the rest______________|
   0            64TB                                            ~120TB

The size of padding region is controlled by
CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_MEMORY_PHYSICAL_PADDING, which is 10 TB by default.

The above issue only exists when
CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_MEMORY_PHYSICAL_PADDING is set to a non-zero value,
which is the case when CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG is enabled. Otherwise,
using __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT doesn't affect KASLR.

Fix it by replacing __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT with MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS.

 [ bp: Massage commit message. ]

Fixes: b83ce5ee9147 ("x86/mm/64: Make __PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT always 52")
Signed-off-by: Baoquan He <bhe@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@suse.de>
Reviewed-by: Thomas Garnier <thgarnie@google.com>
Acked-by: Kirill A. Shutemov <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Cc: "H. Peter Anvin" <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
Cc: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: frank.ramsay@hpe.com
Cc: herbert@gondor.apana.org.au
Cc: kirill@shutemov.name
Cc: mike.travis@hpe.com
Cc: thgarnie@google.com
Cc: x86-ml <x86@kernel.org>
Cc: yamada.masahiro@socionext.com
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190417083536.GE7065@MiWiFi-R3L-srv

diff --git a/arch/x86/mm/kaslr.c b/arch/x86/mm/kaslr.c
index 3f452ffed7e9..d669c5e797e0 100644
--- a/arch/x86/mm/kaslr.c
+++ b/arch/x86/mm/kaslr.c
@@ -94,7 +94,7 @@ void __init kernel_randomize_memory(void)
 	if (!kaslr_memory_enabled())
 		return;
 
-	kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT - TB_SHIFT);
+	kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS - TB_SHIFT);
 	kaslr_regions[1].size_tb = VMALLOC_SIZE_TB;
 
 	/*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/mm/kaslr.c`**
   - The line calculating the size of the first KASLR region has been modified:
     - **Before:** `kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT - TB_SHIFT);`
     - **After:** `kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS - TB_SHIFT);`
   - This change replaces the use of `__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT` with `MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS` to correctly calculate the size of the direct mapping section.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `kaslr.c` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (`b83ce5ee9147`), which incorrectly set `__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT` to a constant value of 52. This led to an incorrect calculation of the maximum system RAM size, thereby weakening the Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) feature.
- By using `MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS`, the patch ensures that the calculation reflects the actual maximum physical memory supported by the system, which can vary based on the page table configuration (4-level vs. 5-level), thus restoring the intended functionality of KASLR.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT - TB_SHIFT);
```
Reason:
The use of `__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT` was set to a constant value of 52, which does not accurately reflect the maximum physical memory supported by the system. This caused the calculation of the size of the direct mapping section to be incorrect, leading to a weakened KASLR when the actual system RAM exceeded 4 PB.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
kaslr_regions[0].size_tb = 1 << (MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS - TB_SHIFT);
```
Reason:
Replacing `__PHYSICAL_MASK_SHIFT` with `MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS` allows the calculation to correctly account for the actual maximum physical memory supported by the system, thus ensuring that the size of the direct mapping section is accurate and KASLR remains effective even with larger amounts of RAM.
